research_problem: Mass assignment (auto-binding) vulnerabilities in REST APIs lack any automated black-box detection approach
technical_approach: From OpenAPI: CRUD semantics from HTTP methods, EM clustering of stemmed parameter vectors to group operations by resource, resource-id heuristic, read-only fields = read outputs never in create/update inputs; update/create-injection test templates; oracle checks overwrite with two distinct values
primary_contribution: First automated black-box mass assignment testing approach (RestTestGen strategy)
dataset_benchmark: 5 open-source REST APIs (VAmPI, OWASP, Toggle, Bookstore, CRUD; 47 operations, 4 languages) with existing + seeded vulnerabilities and safe versions; 10 Google API specs (454 operations) for static scalability
evaluation_metrics: Correctness of CRUD/clustering/resource-id vs gold standard; TP/FP/FN, precision, recall; analysis time
key_findings: CRUD 98%, clustering 94%, resource-id 93%; zero false positives, all vulnerabilities found except 0.4 average FN on OWASP; 5 extra distinct 500-bugs; Google specs analysed in 37.2 s yielding 981 read-only candidates
author_limitations: Gold-standard subjectivity; open-source only; heuristic inference may be imprecise (manual annotation possible)
analyst_limitations: ~10 vulnerabilities, majority self-seeded in exactly the pattern detected (circularity); specs manually corrected; blind to fields absent from read schemas; RQ3 static only, candidate precision unknown; role-agnostic; no baseline; preprint version read
reproducibility: Open-source in RestTestGen; replication package; local SUTs
suggested_extensions: LLM/observation-based sensitive-field discovery without specs; role-aware unified oracle with BOLA/BFLA; real (non-seeded) REST security benchmark; large-scale candidate precision; white-box ORM-based hybrid
evidence_location: Approach p.3-6; setting p.6-7 Table II; RQ1 p.8; RQ2 p.9 Table IV; RQ3 p.9; threats p.8
integrity: Two-column reading order partly scrambled; tables column-split; Template 2 formula partly lost
